installation.note: diff is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: diff compares files and directories, showing the differences between them. It's essential for version control, code reviews, configuration changes, and finding what changed between file versions. Output can be used to create patches.

syntax.description: Compare FILE1 and FILE2, showing differences. Lines starting with < are from FILE1, > are from FILE2.

options.use_case: Show differences in unified format (most common)
Treat uppercase and lowercase as same
Quick check if files are different

examples.title: Compare two files
examples.output:
1,3c1,3
< line1
< line2
< line3
---
> newline1
> newline2
> newline3

breakdown.format: Change: c, Delete: d, Add: a

breakdown.removed: Lines with < are in first file but not second

breakdown.added: Lines with > are in second file but not first

output_explanation.notes: Shows differences. < = from first file, > = from second file. Use diff -u for more readable format.

examples.title: Unified format (readable)

output_explanation.notes: Unified format is more readable. - = removed, + = added. Most common format for code reviews and patches.

examples.use_case: Compare files in readable format (code reviews, patches)

elements.meaning: Recursive - compares all files in directories

breakdown.common: Very useful for comparing project versions, backups

output_explanation.notes: Compares all files in directories recursively. Shows which files differ and how. Very useful for comparing project versions.

examples.title: Quick check if files differ
examples.description: Only report if files are different

elements.meaning: Brief - only says if files differ

breakdown.useful: Quick check without seeing all differences
breakdown.scripts: Perfect for scripts - exit code 0 if same, 1 if different

output_explanation.notes: Only reports if files differ, not how. Perfect for quick checks and scripts. Exit code: 0 = same, 1 = different.

examples.use_case: Quick check if files are different (scripts, automation)

related_commands.relationship: Apply diff; diff creates patches, patch applies them
related_commands.description: Apply patch files created by diff

related_commands.relationship: Version control; git uses diff internally
related_commands.description: Version control (uses diff for showing changes)

best_practices: Use diff -u for readable output (most common)
Use diff -q for quick checks in scripts
Redirect output to create patches: diff -u file1 file2 > patch.diff
Use diff to review configuration changes
performance_tips: diff is fast for most files
Can be slow for very large files or directory trees

additional_notes.unified_format: Use diff -u for readable format. Most common for code reviews and patches.
additional_notes.exit_code: Exit code 0 = files same, 1 = files differ. Useful for scripts.
additional_notes.patches: diff output can be saved and applied with patch command
additional_notes.common_patterns: Very common: diff -u file1 file2 (compare), diff -r dir1 dir2 (directories), diff -q file1 file2 (quick check)
